newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to start selling Kremlin foreign car pool.
newsitem.headline: Russia to start selling Kremlin foreign car pool.

text.p: A Russian trading exchange will auction off the first group of imported foreign limousines next month in line with a government decision to make ministers and other officials drive home-built cars.

Interfax news agency quoted the head of the Russian Exchange as saying that the first 30 cars on sale would come from the Kremlin car pool. The exchange is one of several offering a wide range of goods for sale by auction.
The initiative to buy Russian cars came from new First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who was previously the governor of the auto-making centre of Nizhny Novgorod.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin then latched onto the idea, using it as a key part of a recent "Buy Russian" campaign and a tough drive to eliminate corruption amongst civil servants.
Kremlin business managers had objected to the idea of selling off the foreign cars, saying they were far more reliable than their Russian equivalents.
